title: Tracking Temporal Changes in Metal Pollution in Estuarine Sediments: Population Pressure, Pollution Trends, and Policy Responses in India, China, and the USA
content:
Abstract

This study introduces the Population Normalized Pollution Load (PNPL) as a complementary approach to the Pollution Load Index (PLI) to evaluate sediment metal contamination in relation to population pressure. A global comparative assessment of sediment metal contamination was conducted across major estuarine systems from India, China, and the United States using published data sets. The PLI ranked the investigated estuaries from least to most polluted as: Galveston Bay < Yellow River Estuary < Hudson Estuary < Hooghly (Ganga) Estuary < Mahanadi Estuary < Yangtze Estuary < Chesapeake Bay < Pearl River Estuary < Cochin Estuary < Ulhas Estuary. Temporal PLI trends revealed contrasting contamination trajectories, which reflected differences in historical pollution intensity, population pressure, and pollution control practices. The combined PLI–PNPL assessment indicated declining population-normalized contamination intensity in estuaries such as Mahanadi, Hooghly, Hudson River, and Galveston Bay, while Ulhas and Cochin continued to exhibit elevated contamination burdens. This study also assessed historical and ongoing environmental monitoring and pollution-control programs and their potential influence on sediment metal pollution, highlighting the need for sustained monitoring, effective wastewater management, and consistent policy implementation. The combined use of PLI and PNPL provided a more comprehensive assessment of estuarine contamination by considering both the overall sediment pollution burden and the associated population pressure. This approach could be adopted in future studies to provide a broader understanding of estuarine contamination patterns.
